lines.text: Resection of the terminal ileum is associated with malabsorption of which of the following substances?
Meet the terminal ileum, the recycling truck of the gut. It carries bile salts back home.
Then the scissors cut it away. That is a resection, for example in Crohn's disease.
(sigh) The yellow bile salts spill out and are lost.
Without the terminal ileum, the enterohepatic circulation breaks, so bile salts become deficient.
The worried gallbladder fills with cholesterol gallstones, the clinical consequence.
Remember: resect the terminal ileum and you lose bile salts, with a higher risk of cholesterol gallstones.
A patient with a six centimetre abdominal aortic aneurysm is scheduled for elective repair, and an echocardiogram is requested. The ejection fraction is defined as what?
The answer is the ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume.
Our smiling patient has a six centimetre aortic aneurysm, waiting for elective repair.
Before surgery, the echocardiogram checks how well his heart pumps.
In diastole the ventricle fills to about one hundred and twenty millilitres. This full bucket is the end-diastolic volume.
In systole the heart pours out about seventy millilitres into the cup. That is the stroke volume.
(laugh) So the ejection fraction is simply the cup divided by the bucket.
Remember: ejection fraction is the ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume.
